title: Customer-bridge throttling and adaptive fast-fail shim for Hosted API 5xx/timeouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: After two customer escalations last week we observed correlated 5xx waves and long-tail timeouts caused by a combination of tenant-fanout, cold KV-cache thrashing, and synchronous downstream retries. This ticket implements a two-part defensive mechanism: (1) a customer-bridge path for prioritized customers that routes a small percentage of requests to a stretched fastpath (reserved capacity or compatible model variant) with explicit SLA handling and (2) an adaptive fast-fail/shim in the edge admission layer that detects tenant-level failure amplification and proactively returns a controlled fast-fail (429/503 with retry-after/X-retry-id) for non-priority traffic while preserving telemetry needed for postmortem. Goal: stop global retry amplification, protect high-value customers during escalations, and reduce 5xx storm surface while maintaining signal for root-cause analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Edge admission implements per-tenant adaptive windowing that transitions from allow -> slowpath -> fast-fail based on configurable error-rate and p95 latency thresholds
Customer-bridge routing exists as an opt-in policy per-tenant with the ability to pin to: hosted-reserved-fastpath, dedicated-fallback, or model-variant-fallback
During synthetic failure tests we show a 60% reduction in end-to-end 5xx amplification for non-bridge tenants and zero customer-visible outage for three pilot customers on the bridge
Observability: dashboards for in-flight counts, fast-fail transitions, bridge-forwarded RPS, and per-tenant retry-ids are live and diagnostic traces link to the fast-fail decision
Runbook: one-click rollback and gated rollout via console feature-flags; postmortem template created
Automated e2e tests in CI simulate tenant surge + cold-kv cache and validate no regression for streaming paths
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): enable edge-adaptive-fastfail in us-east with 5% of routed traffic (internal customers only)
Phase 1 (pilot): opt-in 3 pilot customers to customer-bridge in us-east and eu-west, observe 48h
Phase 2 (staggered): increase adaptive-fastfail coverage to 50% while enabling bridge for top-10 revenue tenants
Phase 3 (global): enable by default with sensible defaults and trunked telemetry after 2 successful weeks
Rollback: console feature flag to disable adaptive-fastfail and bridge routing; kill-switch endpoint added to ops runbook
mitigation_steps: Immediate: deploy temporary rate-limit at edge for multi-part uploads to block largest amplification vector
Next 24h: enable per-tenant request fingerprinting to avoid duplicate replay during incident investigations
Post-deploy: keep a 24/7 pager window for first 48h of canary, with escalation path to runtime-oncall and SRE
Customer comms: draft proactive emails for bridged customers and templated support responses for affected non-bridged customers
test_plan: Unit tests for admission policy transitions (allow/slowpath/fast-fail) and idempotency token propagation
Integration: simulated tenant surge harness (open-source tool adapted) that hits edge -> router -> runtime with adjustable latencies and kv-eviction patterns
Chaos test: network partitioning between router and runtime to ensure controlled fast-fail does not create more retries
Load test: validate no regression in p50/p95 latency for streaming endpoints with adaptive-fastfail enabled
